blockers.title: Monthly spend limit reached — six agents killed mid-flight
blockers.body: Six subagents terminated with "You've hit your monthly spend limit": the RPE critic, the meet-engine critic, the e1RM rework builder, the fatigue builder, the streak builder, and the sprite builder. Two had begun work; neither had committed anything usable and both worktrees were discarded.
blockers.consequence: No further builders or critics can be dispatched until the limit is raised. Everything merged so far is intact and green — 278 tests across four modules — but three merged modules were never graded, and the whole art/UI half of the run never started. Nothing here is lost; it is paused. Raising the limit resumes it from exactly this state.

blockers.title: Reference material cannot be retrieved in this sandbox
blockers.body: Egress policy allows the npm registry and GitHub, and WebSearch returns text results. Everything else — Wikipedia/Wikimedia, openpowerlifting.org, sprite archives, image hosts — is refused at the proxy with a 403 on CONNECT. No image, video, or PDF reference can be fetched.
blockers.consequence: Every GDD §12.2 bar that requires blind A/B against real reference art is structurally unverifiable here: lifter sprites, gym/environment art, result card vs. real federation sheets, anime cut-ins, and meet-day tension vs. broadcast footage. Per CLAUDE.md these are reported unverifiable rather than passed on reasoning alone. More loop rounds cannot fix this — it needs reference files supplied locally.

blockers.title: GDD §6.3 contradicts CLAUDE.md on decreasing attempt weight
blockers.body: CLAUDE.md states attempts may not go down in weight within a lift. GDD §6.3 offers, after a miss, to "repeat the weight … vs. drop down (guaranteed banked total, no PR)". Both cannot hold.
blockers.consequence: Real-sport rules side with CLAUDE.md — within a lift a weight may be repeated after a miss but never decreased — so the meet engine enforces non-decreasing and the conflict is flagged rather than silently resolved. If §6.3's "drop down" meant taking a smaller jump rather than going below the last attempt, the GDD wording needs updating; if it meant a real decrease, that is a deliberate departure from the sport and the engine needs changing. Your call — CLAUDE.md forbids me picking one quietly.

pieces.name: Foundation
pieces.bar: Not a GDD bar — infrastructure. Must render, screenshot, and test.
pieces.note: Expo + TS strict + vitest + Skia-on-web + Playwright screenshot harness all verified working end to end.

pieces.name: RPE → %1RM table
pieces.bar: Published RPE charts. Binary and testable — critic verifies against source values.
pieces.note: Merged and green (50 tests). 108-cell Tuchscherer chart cross-checked against two independent transcriptions. Its critic was killed by the spend limit before reporting — this module is built but never independently graded.

pieces.name: e1RM formulas
pieces.bar: Published e1RM formulas. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: SENT BACK by its critic and NOT yet fixed: Epley/Brzycki are rep-max formulas, but GDD §3.3 makes nearly every logged set deliberately submaximal, so RPE could not move e1RM at all for singles. The rework builder was killed by the spend limit before writing anything. This is the top of the queue on resume.

pieces.name: DOTS scoring
pieces.bar: Published DOTS coefficients. Binary and testable.
pieces.note: WINS ITS BAR — the only piece to be graded and pass. All ten coefficients verified by the critic against source bytes it fetched itself from OpenPowerlifting, term order checked by hand two ways. Noted gap: no test pins any DOTS value to anything outside the repo, so a wrong digit at authoring time could not fail the suite.

pieces.name: Meet engine
pieces.bar: Meet structure correctness: order, 3 attempts, non-decreasing weight, best-per-lift total, bomb-out.
pieces.note: Merged and green (76 tests). Typed invariants, no throws, deterministic replay; bomb-out modelled as a distinct outcome rather than a zero. Its critic was killed by the spend limit before reporting — built but never independently graded.

pieces.name: Fatigue / readiness
pieces.bar: Plausible game-feel abstraction. No visible fatigue meter (§12.3).
pieces.note: Builder killed by spend limit before writing anything.

pieces.name: Streak / Recovery Days
pieces.bar: Never punishes daily engagement. Manual token use, hold cap, first-break tutorial.
pieces.note: Builder killed by spend limit before writing anything.

pieces.name: Tuning constants
pieces.bar: Every game-feel value a named constant in one place. Enforced by a magic-number audit.

pieces.name: Progression boundary
pieces.bar: No client-authoritative progression writes. Shaped for Edge Functions.

pieces.name: Lift input mechanic
pieces.bar: The lift must feel good (GDD pillar 1).
pieces.note: Feel is not judgeable by any critic — GDD §12.1 says so outright. Deliverable is a tunable artifact, not a verdict.

pieces.name: Lifter sprites & animation
pieces.bar: Blind A/B against real 16-bit SNES/Genesis sprite work. Maximal attempt must animate heavier.
pieces.note: Builder killed by spend limit after starting a palette; nothing committed, worktree discarded. Reference for its bar is also unreachable here.

pieces.name: Gym / environment art
pieces.bar: Blind A/B, same era. Readability at phone scale.
pieces.note: Reference unreachable — bar will report unverifiable.

pieces.name: Daily session loop
pieces.bar: Duolingo-class session. Time-to-first-input, session length, close-out moment.
pieces.note: Absolute metrics measurable; blind A/B against the real app is not.

pieces.name: Meet day
pieces.bar: Dread and anticipation comparable to a real third-attempt walkout.
pieces.note: Broadcast footage unreachable — bar will report unverifiable.

pieces.name: Result card
pieces.bar: Would a competitive lifter believe ours is real? vs. real federation sheets.
pieces.note: Real sheets unreachable — bar will report unverifiable.

pieces.name: Cross-module inconsistency (found, unfixed)
pieces.bar: The four modes must feel like one game — the smoothing-pass concern.
pieces.note: The DOTS critic caught it while grading something else: meet.ts models a bomb-out as total: null, while dots.ts assumes a bomb-out arrives as 0. Two modules disagree about the shape of the same event. Real bug, recorded, not yet fixed.
